reading.identification: A surviving 'penshuisje' — one of the row of tiny tripe-sellers' shops built 1542-43 as a shallow 2.5 m lean-to against the north flank of Ghent's Groot Vleeshuis on Pensmarkt — two low storeys of weathered grey limestone rubble under small crow-stepped street-facing gables, ground floor a shop (latterly a frituur), currently shored and hoarded for restoration.
reading.notes:
Identification is anchored by the site's own interpretation panel (set B, image 1): the penshuisjes of 1542 beside the Groot Vleeshuis, the last surviving one now a frituur. Set A (3D tiles) is unusable — the whole range dissolves into untextured purple mush, so nothing below was read from it.

MASSING: do not extrude as a freestanding block. footprint_m 13.4 x 2.5 with area 32 m2 is a lean-to strip against the Vleeshuis flank; the rear wall is party wall (attached_neighbours 1) and the far taller Vleeshuis roof rises behind these small gables. An isolated 9 m box would read wrong from any rotated camera — this is exactly the visible-primitive failure.

ROOF: seen clearly in the enlarged crop — a repeating run of crow-stepped gable ends (trapgevels) with small stone pinnacles, each gable perpendicular to the street, hence ridge_parallel_to_street false. A green-slated pentice/penthouse roof slope runs below them; worth generating as geometry, it is a strong horizontal wedge at ~5-6 m and will matter for street-level scatter.

MATERIAL: wall is coursed grey limestone/sandstone rubble (Tournai bluestone with Balegem dressings), badly eroded, with brick patching and a whitewashed brick plinth at the near end. 'marble' is chosen as the closest available dielectric proxy for limestone (eps' ~7) — 'brick' (~3.75) and 'concrete' (~5.24) both understate it. roughness_mm 10 reflects genuinely rough rubble with deeply weathered raked joints; this is the 1-10 cm regime and must stay a roughness number, never meshed relief. trim 'wood' for the heavy timber ground-floor front, lintel beam and window joinery, which is what the beam actually meets at street level; note the window surrounds themselves are dressed stone.

GROUND FLOOR marked inferred, not seen: the front is boarded in dark timber and fenced off by white picket hoarding, so shopfront vs blank cannot be resolved from the image. 'shopfront' is the correct standing class given the documented frituur use and the wide timber front with a door opening under a beam.

STOREYS inferred: grade is hidden behind the hoarding so the count cannot be made from the image. 9.0 m is height_source 'no-data', so it is treated as ridge height, not eaves — 3.0 + 2.6 gives eaves ~5.6 m with the steep gable and crow-steps carrying the rest.

TEMPORARY WORKS: the bright yellow steel raking shores are restoration propping, not building geometry. Include them as scaffolding clutter if capture-time fidelity is wanted, but never as facades facets.

CLUTTER: fronting_street is highway=pedestrian with car_access=none — no parked vehicles anywhere on Pensmarkt. Correct clutter for this scene is the site hoarding and Denys signage, wheelie bins, a blue drum, pedestrians, and wet granite setts. Detail budget should go to the gable silhouettes, the crow-steps, the window reveals and the timber ground-floor front; the party-wall side deserves none.
